S66.01.needs: the Desktop app with at least one local folder added
S66.01.note: Cloud sessions use a "Select repository" chip instead of a folder chip; the exact composer position was not traced in the render tree.
steps: Sign in to the Desktop app and click Code in the sidebar.
Click New to start a session, then click the folder chip in the composer.
Pick a folder from the list in the menu.
Check that the chosen folder name stays on the chip before you send, to compare with Expected.
S66.01.where: Sidebar > Code > New > folder chip (local folder menu, "Change the folder")

labels.text: Search or type a branch name

S66.02.needs: a local git folder with more than one branch
S66.02.note: Cloud sessions use the same "Change the branch" label for a repository branch; local switching checks out the branch in the folder.
steps: Open Code, click New, and pick a local folder that is a git repository.
Click the branch chip shown under the folder chip.
Type in "Search or type a branch name" or click a branch in the list, then click "Use this branch".
Check that the chip shows the branch you chose.
S66.02.where: Sidebar > Code > New > branch chip under the folder chip ("Change the branch")

S66.04.needs: a paid account for the Cloud option
S66.04.note: Cloud sandbox execution is unfinished: it depends on the E2B switch (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts). Whether the Cloud option actually runs in a sandbox today was not verified; the exact selector position was not traced.
steps: Click Code, then New.
Open the environment choice in the composer and look for "Local" and "Cloud".
Select "Cloud" and check that the composer changes to repository controls.
Select "Local" and check that the folder chip returns.
S66.04.where: Sidebar > Code > New > environment selector ("Local" or "Cloud")

S66.05.needs: the Desktop app with a folder allowed to run commands
S66.05.note: A folder shows no sessions until its command access is allowed; the empty-state text is "No coding sessions on this device yet."
steps: Sign in to the Desktop app and click Code in the sidebar.
Look for the "Your computer" section and the "On this device" list.
Click a session row to open it.
Check that the session opens and its title is shown, to compare with Expected.

S66.06.note: Cloud sessions also have a "Rename" item (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts). The exact text of the More actions label was built from a function, not a fixed string.
steps: Open a session from Your computer.
Click the "More actions for" control on the session row (its name is the session title).
Click Rename and type a new name in the "Session name" field.
Check that the new title shows in the list and the session header.
S66.06.where: Sidebar > Code > Your computer > session row > More actions > Rename

S66.07.needs: a Desktop app session with a task that asks for approval
S66.07.note: Visible copy for failed and closed states was not found in the status labels read; "Approval required" appears on the approval card (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts), not as a status word.
steps: Open Code and look at the "Your computer" list.
Start a task in a session and watch the row change to "Running".
Wait for the run to end and check the row shows "Ready" or "Idle".
Check that a session with an archived state shows "Archived".
S66.07.where: Sidebar > Code > Your computer (status words on each session row)

S66.11.needs: a Desktop app session with a text file in its folder
S66.11.note: The exact button position in the session panel was not traced; the editor code is in apps/web/features/code/components/LocalFileEditor.tsx.
steps: Open a Desktop app session whose folder has a text file.
Click Files (or press Command P) and open the file.
Click Edit, change a line, then click Save.
Check that the change shows in the file and that the file on disk changed.
S66.11.where: Sidebar > Code > Your computer > session > Files > open a file > Edit > Save

S66.15.needs: a Desktop app session with a local folder
S66.15.note: The terminal is LocalTerminal.tsx; the exact dock position was not traced in the render tree.
steps: Open a Desktop app session.
Click Terminal, or open Session actions > Open in > Terminal.
Click the "Run a command" field, type a short command such as ls, and click Run.
Check that the output appears under the terminal.
S66.15.where: Code > local session > Terminal (also Session actions > Open in > Terminal)

labels.text: No commands have run in this session.

S66.17.needs: a Desktop app session with a local folder
S66.17.note: The exit status is kept in LocalTerminal.tsx (exitCode) but its visible wording was not found; check it on screen.
steps: Open a Desktop app session and click Terminal.
Check that the empty text "No commands have run in this session." shows if nothing ran.
Run a command, then look at the list of commands with their output.
Check that each entry shows the command and its result, to compare with Expected.
S66.17.where: Code > local session > Terminal (empty text "No commands have run in this session.")

S66.18.needs: a git folder with a changed file
S66.18.note: The diff renderer (CodeDiffFile.tsx, LocalChangesPanel.tsx) was not read line by line; the "Changes" button label was confirmed from the test file apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionPanel.test.tsx.
steps: Open a Desktop app session in a git folder and make a change to a file (a task or an edit).
Click the "Changes" button in the session.
Click a changed file in the Changes panel.
Check that the line-by-line diff shows removed and added lines, to compare with Expected.
S66.18.where: Code > local session > Changes (the Changes panel, then pick a changed file)

S66.19.needs: a git folder with several changed files
S66.19.note: The words for created, modified or deleted per file were not found in the labels read; check the file rows on screen.
steps: Open a session with several changed files.
Click the "Changes" button.
Look at the commit line "Commits N of M changed files" and the "Include in the commit:" choices.
Untick one file and check the count changes.
S66.19.where: Code > local session > Changes (file list with commit choices)

S66.24.needs: a Desktop app session with a local folder
S66.24.note: The hint says Plan changes nothing; the approval step after the plan was not traced.
steps: Open a Desktop app session and click the "Permissions" chip (it shows the current mode, such as Ask).
Choose "Plan" and read the hint "Reads and plans. Changes nothing."
Send a request that would edit a file, and check the agent proposes a plan and does not change files.
Check the plan waits for approval before any edit, to compare with Expected.
S66.24.where: Code > local session > the Permissions chip > Plan (cloud: Approval mode > Mode > Plan)

S66.25.needs: a Desktop app session with a local folder
S66.25.note: The visible word is "Auto", not "agent mode". In the cloud composer the same control is labelled "Approval mode" (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts).
steps: Open a Desktop app session and click the "Permissions" chip.
Read the choices: Ask, Auto, Plan, Bypass permissions.
Choose "Auto" and read the hint "Edits files without asking. Asks before commands and git hook or MCP changes."
Send a small edit request and check it edits without asking, to compare with Expected.
S66.25.where: Code > local session > the Permissions chip > Auto (or Ask)

S66.26.needs: a Desktop app session with a local folder
S66.26.note: The cloud Approval mode options are Ask, Auto and Skip. Whether the running session honours each mode was not verified.
steps: Open a Desktop app session and click the "Permissions" chip.
Pick "Ask" and send a task that runs a command; check it asks for approval.
Pick "Auto", then "Bypass permissions", and send the same task.
Check the approval prompts follow each mode, to compare with Expected.
S66.26.where: Code > local session > Permissions chip (Ask / Auto / Plan / Bypass permissions); cloud: Approval mode chip

S66.27.needs: a signed-in account with an open session
S66.27.note: The ring is UsageRing in apps/web/features/code/components/CodeComposer.tsx; it shows the context window only when the model size is known.
steps: Open a session in the composer.
Click the small usage ring button (aria label "Usage").
Read the "Context window" line in the popover.
Send a message and reopen the popover to check the used amount rises.
S66.27.where: Code > composer > Usage ring button (popover shows "Context window")

S66.28.note: If usage data is missing the popover shows "Usage is not available right now." (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts).
steps: Open the composer in Code.
Click the "Usage" ring button.
Read "Plan usage limits", "Five hour limit" and "Weekly, all models", and "See detailed breakdown".
Check the bars and reset times match your plan, to compare with Expected.
S66.28.where: Code > composer > Usage ring button > "Plan usage limits"

labels.text: Push and open a pull request
Open a pull request on GitHub

S66.36.needs: a GitHub-connected repository, a non-default branch, and a linked GitHub account
S66.36.note: Panel placement was not traced; the panel component is apps/web/features/code/components/LocalPullRequest.tsx. Some states show a reason instead when a pull request is not possible.
steps: Open a Desktop app session in a GitHub-connected repository on a non-default branch.
Look for the "Push and open a pull request" action in the session.
Click it, then check the pull request number ("Pull request #") and state (open, draft, merged or closed) appear.
Open "Open a pull request on GitHub" to compare the link with the panel.
S66.36.where: Code > local session > "Push and open a pull request" (on a branch other than the default)

S66.38.needs: a Desktop app session in a folder with a test command
S66.38.note: The button position was not traced in the session panel; if no test command is found, the text "No test command found here" appears.
steps: Open a Desktop app session in a folder with a test script in package.json.
Click "Run tests".
Watch for "Running <command>" and then the result line such as "<command> passed." or "<command> failed with exit code N."
Open "Test output" and check the failing output appears, to compare with Expected.
S66.38.where: Code > local session > Run tests (results under "Test output")

S66.40.note: Sharing options shown as "Shared with your team" and "Shared by link" (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts). The share dialog file is apps/web/features/code/components/CodeShareDialog.tsx; the exact opening path was not traced end to end.
steps: Open a cloud session in Code.
Click "Session actions" and choose "Share".
In the "Share session" dialog, pick the sharing option and copy the link.
Sign in with a second account in the same workspace (or open the link) and check the session opens, to compare with Expected.
S66.40.where: Code > session > Session actions > Share (dialog "Share session")

S66.41.needs: a paired desktop app signed into the same account
S66.41.note: "Continue in VS Code" also appears in the session panel (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionPanel.tsx). The Desktop item shows only when a desktop is paired; the phone route was not checked.
steps: Open a session in Code in the web app or Desktop app.
Click "Session actions", then hover or click "Open in".
Choose "Desktop app" and check the session opens in the desktop app.
Check the same session is shown with the same transcript, to compare with Expected.
S66.41.where: Code > session > Session actions > Open in > Desktop app (or Open in > Terminal)
